synopsis: Volvo CE’s wheel-loader Collision Mitigation System was announced on 11 January 2023, developed in-house and patent-pending; its documented scope was reverse-only operation at 3–15 km/h, with braking lasting 2–3 seconds [f10625, f1379, f1238]. The corpus treats this restricted scope on selected models as a precedent for staged release, while noting that Volvo reports these loaders spend 40–50% of their time reversing and documents conditions for switching intervention off [f10973, f73, f10630, f11167]. The system remembers the last slope climbed to avoid braking when reversing down a stockpile, but no independent performance test was found, and published weather limits, false-intervention rates and validation methods were absent [f11392, f1242, f11394]. An April 2025 announcement covered new-generation L150, L180, L200 High Lift, L220 and L260 wheel loaders [f1385]. For virtual development, an undated MathWorks story describes Volvo CE’s real-time human-in-the-loop excavator simulator built with Simulink and Simscape; such simulators may be needed for warning-then-brake human factors [f8391, f9379]. Volvo reports fewer prototypes and shorter lead time, describing physical prototypes as costing millions of dollars and months, but this evidence is qualitative rather than controlled cross-vendor benchmarking [f8737, f8738, f8315].
